Your complaint 3 — “that is just wrong… it is the lighting path”. Ground vehicles were the only object class that never filled in its lighting data before drawing, so the shader took a “no lights here” shortcut and drew them at full raw texture brightness — completely unlit. They now populate a per-object light row like everything else. Direction matters and it cuts both ways: brighter in daylight, noticeably DARKER at night. The night direction is the one most likely to read as a regression, so look at vehicles at night beside mechs first.

Shoreline: DISPLACEMENT, FACETING, or the third thing?
still a one-word answer — but the question has changed since it was first written

Look at the mc2_17 waterline and say which you are seeing. (a) DISPLACEMENT — the edge is in the wrong place, cutting across land or sea. (b) FACETING — the edge is in the right place but built from visible straight risers instead of a curve. (c) A GLOW TRACING THE TILE GRID — the edge itself is fine, but something bright is drawn along it in steps, worst at night.
You can answer (a) vs (b) from the two plots in §20a without launching anything: they draw the stock waterline against the 128 wu tile lattice for both maps. On mc2_17 the stock line is a smooth sinuous curve that crosses tile boundaries freely; on mc2_10 it is a right-angle staircase locked to the lattice. If what you see on mc2_17 looks like the mc2_10 plot, that is displacement and the offline data is wrong about the map. Caveat stated plainly: those are offline contour plots of the shipping heightfield, not rendered frames — no rendered engine frame of mc2_17 water exists anywhere on disk.

Two corrections since this row was written, and the second one is a live lead.
(1) The arithmetic that used to appear here is withdrawn. This row previously said “the arithmetic says (b): a 128 wu tile projects to ~147 px at the intro camera and you measured risers of 138–148 px”. That px pair has no derivation anywhere in the repo — no script, no measurement JSON, no status doc — and an identical “137–148px” string does exist, in tools/visual_verify/regions/mc2_10_saved_204523.json, describing mc2_10 at a top-down pose. (2) A default-ON candidate cause that all six shoreline lanes missed. MC2_TERRAIN_SHORELINE has three readers and they disagree: gos_terrain_lod_chunk.cpp:2659 and mclib/terrain.cpp:1120 both read !(v && v[0]=='0') → default ON, while gos_TerrainLodChunk_IsShorelineMaskActive() at gos_terrain_lod_chunk.cpp:3903 reads (v && v[0] && v[0]!='0') → default OFF. That third reader is the one that suppresses the legacy screen-space runShoreline() pass (gos_postprocess.cpp:3404). Because it is false on an unset environment, the suppression never fires and the legacy glow runs on every stock frame with water, alongside the V3 band it was supposed to replace. The engine’s own comment at :2659 says that legacy pass “traced the raw tile-quantized water-mesh edge and amplified the staircase at night”. Chain re-verified end to end for this page. If your answer is (c), that is where the fix is, and it is a one-line change.

sections.heading: 8. Static prop self-shadowing (buildings read flat / cardboard)

blocks.html: User report (mc2_10 night): a building's light-facing parts are FULLY lit and its away-facing parts dark, but nothing accounts for occlusion by the building's own geometry — a wall behind a taller wing, a recessed courtyard, an inset doorway or the underside of an overhang all render full-bright.

blocks.html: NO CODE CHANGE WAS NEEDED — and none was made. Both mechanisms were already shipped and simply switched off. Root cause is three stacked things: (1) static_prop.frag writes the a=0.25 "no self shadow" GBuffer class and shadow_screen.frag deliberately skips the dynamic cascade for it ("CPU never self-shadowed buildings"); (2) the baked base light is a per-LEAF constant (GetARGBHighlight(), one scalar per TG_Shape), so it adds no intra-surface variation, and calc_light has no occlusion term at all; (3) what is left is a pure per-face max(N·L,0) — precisely "fully lit or dark, nothing between". Props already cast into the CSM cascades, so no caster-set widening was required and the alpha-card foliage exclusion was never touched.

Why BOTH gates. MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE opts props back into the dynamic cascade — that gives coarse wing-on-wing shadow, but the cascades are map-sized and cannot resolve a doorway reveal. MC2_SSAO adds the fine contact term (recesses, inside corners, undersides) using depth + GBuffer normals props already write. Measured on mc2_01 day: RECEIVE alone changes 0.25-0.73% of pixels and 100% of them get DARKER, zero brighter (a pure occlusion term can only darken — animation or a lighting bug could not be one-sided); adding SSAO multiplies coverage 20-60x (to 1.5-14.7%) while staying ~99% darker.

Night building, mc2_10 composed close pose — OFF (top) vs BOTH gates ON (bottom). Look at the penthouse/roof-deck junction, under the parapet lip, the recessed window bays, the inside corner where the near wing meets the rear block, and the garage doorway.
Night compound walls + domes — OFF (top) vs RECEIVE only (bottom): dome flanks, the crevice between adjacent domes, and buttress slopes darken.
Day quantitative pose (mc2_01 airport, full frame)

At mc2_10 night the sibling LIGHT-REALISM-1 sweeping-searchlight animation contaminates cross-launch comparison: pose compound_mid shows 6.66% of pixels changed of which 5.19% get BRIGHTER — that is animation, not this gate. The night verdict above is therefore categorical (a named recess that was flat is now visibly darker), and the clean quantitative pass is the day table, whose zero-brighter distribution independently corroborates the mechanism. Also: all six saved mc2_10 night bookmarks are distant overviews (alt 4954-6045) that cannot resolve intra-building occlusion, so four close poses were composed over the tower/compound complex and archived alongside these images. Verify-by-exaggeration was done by stacking the two gates — neither exposes a strength knob (the 0.4 shadow floor is hard-coded) and the shadow-classification debug view is key-toggled only, unreachable headless.

RESIDUAL — this is why neither gate should default ON yet. Alpha-test lattice props self-shadow as solid slabs: the shadow depth pass has no alpha discard, so a chain-link fence writes a solid depth slab into the cascades and then, with RECEIVE ON, samples that slab and darkens uniformly across the whole lattice (image below — it is the single densest diff region on the day poses). Foliage is protected from this by setRecipeNoShadow; fences and railings are not foliage and are not excluded. The clean fix needs a distinct GBuffer1.a class for alpha-test props so they can be excluded from receive — that edits the render-contract mask encoding shared with shadow_screen.frag, too wide to land unverified, so it is logged as follow-up PROP-ALPHA-SHADOW-CLASS-1 rather than guessed at here. The cheap alternative (marking alpha-test recipes noShadow) is wrong — it would also stop fences casting onto terrain.

⚠ REVIEW-LANES-LOG-2 CORRECTION — prop self-shadow CANNOT fix the building-face complaint, and MC2_SSAO is broken rather than merely off. Three corrections to this section. (1) A face turned away from the sun already has ndl = 0; a shadow term multiplying zero changes nothing, so MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE is architecturally incapable of addressing it — measured, it moves 0.005-0.183% of pixels and only on props like aircraft. (2) The follow-up premise that base_light was the culprit is falsified: a gate built on it was byte-identical at strength 1.0, which multiplies the seed by zero — base_light is effectively ZERO on these props, day and night. The term that actually lights them is ambientTerm, the orientation-free per-actor object-light ambient; that is the real cure site. (3) MC2_SSAO is latent-broken, not off: the AO buffer is white (mean 254.99/255) because aoRadius_ is 3.0 world units against a 42.67 wu map cell — 2% of one cell — and there is no blur pass at all, only a 4-tap box over ±0.5 of a half-res texel, which cannot denoise a 16-sample stochastic kernel. Raising the radius alone therefore trades no-occlusion for visible dither. The 20-60× coverage figure quoted above should not be relied on. (SHADOW-DECISIONS-1, SSAO-RETUNE-1, PROP-BASE-LIGHT-DIR-1.)

blocks.html: Root cause. The min-screen-size clamp added by f412423e was max(1.0, kLbMinNdc / sil) with no upper bound. sil falls off as 1/distance, so k grew without limit and pinned every fixture to a constant hard-edged bright block at every camera distance. Holding a constant screen size was the clamp's literal intent — correct at playable RTS range, which is what made the lights visible at grazing angles — but past that range several hundred regularly-spaced fixtures simply never shrink. Regular spacing + constant size = the dashes. A secondary error compounded it ~1.5x: kLbRefRadius was the authored top-cap radius (0.8), but the rigid billboard maps local Z (the 2.85-unit post axis) onto toCam, so the post foreshortens and the viewer actually sees the local XY cross-section (runwaylight.ase extents 2.015 x 2.326, radius ~1.2). The clamp was sizing against a feature that is never on screen.

Fix. clamp(kLbMinNdc/sil, 1.0, kLbMaxScale) with kLbMaxScale = 2.5 and the corrected reference radius — the legitimate win survives (fixtures still rasterise at playable range) but they resume normal 1/distance shrink and go sub-pixel at overview on their own. Plus the gate is now default-OFF so stock is what ships.

Measured (changed px, |d|>8, BEFORE vs opt-in): overview 549 px in a 136 x 13 horizontal band, 95% of them darker, max delta 240 — that band is the streak. Oblique airbase 9019 px; near-top-down 1817 px. Close ground-level: 0 px, max delta 0 — byte-identical, proving the cap is inactive at close range and gameplay-zoom appearance is untouched.

Goldens are unaffected. v0.5.2-baseline-PROPOSED was blessed at 16c2244a, which predates this gate entirely, so the goldens encode the gate-absent state — the default-OFF flip keeps them valid and no re-bless is needed for this change.

blocks.html:
The user's ruling: "do 3, in the index.html — also ... by all concrete I mean only the actual concrete ... obviously runways, roads, other overlays etc. are their own layer and are currently handled by the shader." Two arms are built, both default OFF, and presented here to choose from. Neither is recommended by the lane — the frames are the decision.

ARM A MC2_CEMENT_CONCRETE_TONE=1 — each concrete cell keeps its own art; only its base tone is pulled onto one reference. ARM B MC2_CEMENT_CONCRETE_CANON=1 — every plain-concrete tile samples one canonical cell, so concrete cannot change colour tile to tile at all. Both act only on cells passing an explicit is-this-actually-concrete test (near-neutral chroma ≤ 0.20, band luminance within [0.72,1.32] of the family centre).

SCOPE QUESTION ANSWERED — markings do NOT live in the concrete cells. This is what blocked the previous lane, and the ruling is confirmed twice over. From source: the solid-cement map g_cementLayerIndexBySlot that ARM B repoints is built only from slots where isCement && !isAlpha; alpha cells are explicitly skipped when it is filled, and TileIsRoadArt() says it outright — a slot present in that map is "solid cement, not road". Runway and road art arrives either as an &Overlays id (its own sampler and blend, u_overlaySidecar / terrain_overlay.frag) or as a cement-alpha transition cell, which is appended past the solid range both arms operate on. From measurement: the cement atlas was dumped (new MC2_CEMENT_ATLAS_DUMP diagnostic) and inspected — on mc2_24, not one of the 110 solid cells has a single texel more than 45 luma above its band mean (largest excursion ~11). There is no painted marking art in solid concrete cells to erase. The census reports family_marked=0; a map that does pack paint into a solid cell is detected (>2% of texels >60 luma above band) and excluded from ARM B by index.

MEASURED — and it reframes the problem. Dumping the atlas showed cross-cell base tone is far more uniform than assumed: on mc2_24 the median cell sits at L=146.3 with p05–p95 = 133–148. What actually varies is inside the cells — 78 of 110 cells carry a large dark region, 36–52% of the tile at L≈60 against concrete at L≈147. That in-cell dark art, not cross-cell tone, is the dominant reason concrete reads as changing colour here. It is why ARM B (which replaces the whole cell) moves ~11–15 luma while ARM A (which only rescales base tone) moves ~1–2.

HONEST CAVEAT ON ARM A — read before grading. On mc2_24 ARM A's census line is family=110 adjusted=96 ref_rgb=149.0,146.4,138.4, which is numerically identical to the census of the gate already rejected (MC2_CEMENT_TONE_MATCH, "after is WAY worse"). On that map every solid cell passes the concrete test, so concrete-only scoping buys nothing and ARM A is that rejected lever with a narrower clamp. It differs only where a map packs genuinely non-concrete cement cells. If mc2_24 is the reference, expect to reject ARM A again — the lane will not claim otherwise.

blocks.html: ARM C — what the “dark regions” actually are

A correction to this section, from measurement. The two arms above were built on the premise that solid concrete cells carry no road or marking art — stated in this pack as “markings do NOT live in the concrete cells”, and supported by a test that found no texel more than 45 luma above its cell band. That test looked only at the bright side. The large dark region it then found in 78 of 110 mc2_24 cells was recorded as “authored material (joints, tarmac, shadowed detail)”.

Dumping the atlas and rendering it shows what it is: a baked asphalt road tileset — straights, curves, T-junctions, crossroads with crosswalk stripes, end caps and a multi-lane highway-with-guardrail piece, painted onto a concrete background. Asphalt is dark, which is precisely why the bright-side test could not see it.

blocks.html:
The reframe this forces — there is no concrete tone problem. Measured with the road texels excluded, the concrete background is already one colour on every map: mc2_24 144.7–149.5 (spread 4.7 luma, std 0.89), mc2_05 3.2, mc2_03 2.4, mc2_10 2.0. mc2_23 and mc2_01 show a ~43-luma span driven entirely by two and one cells, and those cells are wide highway pieces — not concrete.

What makes concrete “magically become a different color” inside a cell is a road: background L≈147 against asphalt L≈82, a ~65-luma hard-edged step. That is exactly the class you scoped out — “obviously runways, roads, other overlays etc. are their own layer and are currently handled by the shader.” True for the &Overlays class. Not true for this one: it is baked into the terrain texture catalog, so TileIsRoadArt() reports “solid cement, not road” and every concrete lever treats a road as concrete.
What ARM C does

ARM C MC2_CEMENT_ROAD_ART_DETECT=1 — detect the baked road art and exclude those cells from every concrete treatment (ARM A's tone pass, ARM B's remap, and the choice of canonical cell). Each cell is split against its own [P60,P95] upper mode — the concrete background — rather than the whole-cell band mean, which on a road-heavy cell is dragged down by the road and hides it. A cell with more than 5% of its texels more than 40 luma below that background is flagged as carrying road art.

ARM C on its own changes no pixels. It writes nothing to the atlas and nothing to the slot→layer map; it only changes which cells ARM A and ARM B are allowed to touch. Its purpose is to make the concrete arms obey your own scope ruling.

What ARM C prevents, measured in-engine. Without it, ARM B repoints 90–100% of the road-carrying cells at its canonical cell — and on 5 of the 6 maps that canonical cell is itself a road tile. On mc2_24 the engine logs canon_cell=10 canon_road_frac=0.312 remapped=109 kept_road=0: ARM B erases every junction, curve and end cap and stamps one straight road segment across every plain concrete tile on the map. With ARM C the same map logs canon_cell=0 canon_road_frac=0.000 remapped=31 kept_road=78 — only the genuinely plain cells are collapsed, and the road network survives intact.

READ THIS FIRST — what would you actually see differently on a default launch? Three things, and nobody has seen any of them. That is the honest answer and it is the most important line in this section. It has changed since this section was first written: it used to say “almost nothing”, because at that moment two of the three had not landed yet.

1. The ground gets brighter on daylight maps. On 21 of 26 campaign missions (plus every multiplayer mc2_m* map) the terrain away from concrete gains a modest albedo-scaled ambient lift — brighter, slightly cooler, a little less contrast between sunlit and shaded ground. Concrete pads deliberately do not move, so the pad-vs-dirt gap you complained about narrows. The five night missions (mc2_05, 10, 19, 21, 23) are bit-for-bit unchanged, because the daylight gate computes to exactly 0.0000 on their authored sun pitch.
2. The pale ring around concrete pads should largely disappear. Transition tiles now sample the pad’s own concrete texture and stop being fogged twice. Side effect: distant concrete reads darker and warmer than it does today.
3. Ground vehicles change brightness in both directions. Trucks, tanks and APCs were being drawn completely unlit at full texture brightness. They now take the same lighting path as everything else, so in daylight they brighten toward the mechs — and at night they will get noticeably DARKER than they are now. That night direction is the change most likely to read as a regression, and it is the one with no prediction, no capture and no measurement behind it. The five night missions are exactly the ones where the terrain ambient floor is OFF, so nothing offsets it.

blocks.html:
The DEFAULT-LAUNCH REALITY note at the top of this page is still accurate — I re-checked every gate it names at the new tip. All seven (MC2_PAVED_OVERLAY_CLASS, MC2_STATIC_PROP_FIXTURE_GLOW, MC2_PROP_BASE_LIGHT_DIR, MC2_SSAO, MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE, MC2_LIGHT_REALISM, MC2_CONE_SPILL_COUPLING) verify OFF. 3ab322a0 briefly flipped MC2_PAVED_OVERLAY_CLASS to default-ON; 2ade84a8 reverted it and a8ea9be5 merged the revert. But the lie did not die — it MOVED, and the new contract cannot catch its new shape. MC2_PAVED_OVERLAY_CLASS’s own registry row is now honest. However two other places assert a false fact about it, both landed after the revert: RendererFeatureRegistry.h (inside MC2_TERRAIN_AMBIENT_FLOOR’s description) and shaders/terrain_lod_chunk.frag:1915 both state the gate “returns 1 when unset … whatever the stale comment above it says”, i.e. that it is live at stock. It is not. 1. Concrete tone & transition tiles
“the transition tiles should just use the same concrete texture”

Root cause found and cured. Eleven earlier lanes attacked the cement atlas and none of them could move it, because the defect was never in the atlas. The overlay layer and the terrain chunk layer disagree on four terms over one physical surface, and the missed one is fog: terrain_overlay.frag carries its own in-shader distance fog toward (0.58,0.65,0.75) clamped at 0.70, terrain_lod_chunk.frag has none, and both layers then receive the shared screen-space edge_fog/fog_oob. The overlay is double-fogged, so the two paths diverge with camera distance. Two pieces of the previous lane's own unexplained data prove it: the seam step grows with distance (runway_ground −4.95 L, runway_mid −16.93 L, runway_overview −14.81 L — only a distance-dependent term can do that), and the overlay pixels are blue-dominant (RenderDoc eid 3678 wrote [0.301,0.3083,0.3623]) which its own warm vec3(0.82,0.80,0.76) tint cannot produce — but the fog colour can.

The cure respects your two rulings. Genuine concrete transition tiles adopt the cement atlas albedo and flat light; tiles carrying authored road or runway art keep their albedo and only get their lighting reconciled — repainting those would be the albedo swap you rejected twice as “WAY worse”. Anything the classifier is unsure about is left entirely alone. The authored marching-squares transition shape is untouched; only the colour inside it moves.

⚠ IT SHIPPED WITH A HOLE, AND THE HOLE WAS THE THING YOU REJECTED TWICE. Two follow-up lanes landed the same day and corrected it three ways. (1) The art guard was wrong twice. The “do not repaint this” mark was first stamped only for 9 of the 17 overlay ids — so a dirt track running onto an apron, or a bridge deck meeting a paved pad, was classified as bare concrete and had its hand-placed art overpainted with plain concrete. Widening it to any overlay id was still not enough: mc2_10's roads and its airbase runway carry no overlay id at all — they are authored as cement-alpha transition art over snow — so they were still being repainted, measured at +46.8 L across 23.0% of the mc2_10 runway frame. That is the albedo swap you rejected twice, arriving through a scoping hole rather than through the gate that owns it. The guard is now the presence of authored art of either kind, and only a cement tile with no authored art at all is repainted. (2) The “identical UV math” claim was not true. The terrain shader insets its atlas sample by half a texel; the adopt path omitted it, so within half a texel of every 128 wu tile border the adopted sample reached into the neighbouring atlas cell — laying a thin wrong-coloured fringe along exactly the borders the change exists to make seamless. Same artifact class as the “weird coloured edge” you reported; it would have traded one edge for another. (3) The killswitch was not clean — it still touched a texture unit when off.

UNVERIFIED — no before/after frame exists. Captures were taken that day, but I checked their manifests: every one measured a binary that does not contain any of these commits. 3. Vehicles not on the same lighting path
“that is just wrong… it is the lighting path”

You were right, and here is the mechanism. Every other object class populates its per-object light row via CacheGpuLightData() before drawing — mechs (mech3d.cpp:5614), buildings (bdactor.cpp:3144/:3181/:4821), trees (:6566), generic props (genactor.cpp:1256). GVAppearance called neither that nor the batcher, yet renders unconditionally through the legacy TG_Shape::Render path, which consumes lightData_ (tgl.cpp:3508) with no gather and no eligibility guard. The chain, each link cited to a committed blob: numLights_ zero-inits (tgl.h:339) → addLightDataStructure is pure dedup/append with no back-fill, so the all-zero row is stored verbatim (txmmgr.cpp:1929-1988) → calc_light takes its numLights.x==0 early return and returns vec3(1,1,1), discarding even the per-vertex base_light (lighting.hglsl:232-236) → the fragment shader multiplies by it. Vehicles drew at raw albedo × 1.0 — completely unlit, day and night. Buildings reach that same legacy path only as a fallback they normally never take, so vehicles were the only class actually exercising an ungathered row.

This also settles the old “trucks are just darker textures” thread: the albedo measurement was right (trucksprop.tga masked luminance 85.9 vs a 787-texture corpus median of 86.2 — 49th percentile, dead average) and the albedo theory was wrong. Mechs and buildings get ambient + sun×ndl, which exceeds 1.0 in daylight, so a median-brightness texture at ×1.0 still looks dark parked beside one. RETRACTED in fc43338a.

The follow-up matters. The first commit lit exactly one leaf per vehicle, because CacheGpuLightData() populates only firstShapeNodeLeaf (correct for the batcher, which broadcasts it; wrong for the legacy path, where TG_MultiShape::Render loops every leaf and each submits its own row). ccb713ae gathers for all leaves.

blocks.html: 20b. Trees, black quads, sunk turrets

Three defects that were not fixed. One had a false closure removed; two are still uncaused. The useful part of all three is the same discovery: the tests that were supposed to cover them cannot reach them.

rows.html:
A previous session closed this as “CLOSED, NO DEFECT — the silhouettes are baked colormap art from burnInShadows”. That closure is now refuted, not merely unsupported — and it left no artifact on disk anywhere, so there was nothing to re-read.

Refuted at source: burnInShadows (mclib/terrtxm2.cpp:609) builds a height map, ray-marches shadows through that, and modulates the colormap. It never touches an object list, an appearance, a TG_Shape, or any prop or tree structure. It cannot produce a tree-shaped silhouette.
Refuted in the texels. The mission's own object list was parsed out of the shipping archive: 2560 objects — 2088 TREE, 241 terrain objects, 219 buildings, 11 turrets, 1 gate. Every one of the 2088 tree positions was tested for a core-vs-ring darkening against the deployed colormap under all 8 orientations (4 rotations × optional mirror), so no orientation choice could rescue the claim. Every reading is within 1.5σ and inside the spread of the random control points; p(core darker) never exceeds 0.541 — a coin flip. The statistic is strong enough to exclude any silhouette of depth ≥20 luminance on more than ~2.4% of the trees.
A structural backstop makes it moot anyway: the stock burn-in is 1280² over 12800 world units — 10 world units per pixel — and a tree card is 2–4 pixels. A recognisable tree silhouette cannot come from that texture at any resolution in the chain.

The real finding, and it is structural. TreeAppearance::update writes the terrain light sample into slot 1, the AMBIENT light (bdactor.cpp:6924) and then deactivates the sun outright — light->active = false at :6938, restored only at :7054, with the static light bake at :7039 sitting inside that window. GatherLightsParameters skips inactive lights (txmmgr.cpp:2488), so a tree's light row contains one AMBIENT entry and no INFINITE entry at all. The shader's sun scan (static_prop.vert:715-728) therefore never finds one and sunColor stays vec3(0.0), which makes the load-bearing line lit = (seed + ambientTerm) * propDirFactor + sunColor * ndl (:823) carry a term that is identically zero for every tree.
Buildings do the opposite — they write to slot 0 and leave the sun active (bdactor.cpp:3856).
Consequence: MC2_PROP_FOLIAGE_ALPHAFLAG, which only changes how ndl is computed, is a guaranteed no-op for trees on a default launch — it is multiplied by zero.

This is not a port regression. Both lines are present in the first commit of the imported Microsoft source. Trees have always been ambient-only. What changed is the consumer: static_prop.vert has no ambient floor and no protective early return, unlike calc_light, which returns vec3(1) when a row is empty.

Nothing shipped. 03519ea1 is one file, +402 lines of markdown, no code, no gate, no build, no launch. Seven discriminating A/B tests are specified and none were run, because launches are blocked. And the lane says the honest thing: “I never saw the user's frame… the single highest-value next step is asking the user which frame.”

The defect, stated precisely for the first time: on BTurretControl and LiaoTurretGenerator the window and vent panels render as solid pure-black quads (RGB 0,0,0) with a dithered 1-bit-alpha fringe, while the same window bands on LiaoHeavyGateControl, the Barracks and the Quonsets render correctly. So a pose that frames only the latter grades nothing — which is exactly what earlier work did. The previous pose set sat inside the same walled compound but at altitude 650, where it framed the perimeter wall and the Quonset row and the defect is simply not in shot.

One cause is ruled out: the far-backdrop path is not it — across six poses there were no black quads to fix. (Those six poses were the wrong frame, which is itself the finding.)
Nothing is ruled in. UNCAUSED.

Uncaused, and worse — barely described. The defect survives on disk as a two-word phrase in a session ledger and a single pose-coverage tag (turret_ground_seating). There is no prose anywhere saying what “sunk” means concretely — how far, which turrets, or a screenshot. UNVERIFIED as a defect description, not just as a fix.

blocks.html: ⚠ THE KEY INSIGHT, and it applies to both of the uncaused defects. The live lead is BldgAppearance::setGesture (mclib/bdactor.cpp:1829-1848): an idle building that is registered as a static prop has its static registration invalidated on its first gesture, because the GPU registry is holding a stale static-pose recipe. It fires at most once per building, ever — bdAnimationState never returns to idle, there is no reset path. No test that has ever run reaches that line. The only entry point is Building::updateAnimations(), whose ~17 gesture calls all sit inside gameplay state switches — sensor-tower contact counts, gate open/close cycles, damage and destruction. The smoke tier is five stock missions, 30 seconds each, idle fly-throughs: no AI engagement, no weapon fire, no gate traversal, so no building ever leaves the idle state and the counter stays zero. This was designed in and disclosed from the start — the 2026-06-03 implementation plan says the path would be “code-reviewed but not runtime-exercised” and told reviewers not to block on it. A fixture that fires a building gesture is the prerequisite for testing this defect class at all. It does not exist.

Two honesty notes on the evidence behind the paragraph above. (1) Seventeen capture arms were run against the airfield (scratch/mc203air/, 6 poses each at 4K) and produced no written verdict of any kind — no status document exists for that lane in any worktree. (2) The anim-gate A/B arm was run without its own instrument switched on: the [ANIM_GATE v1] counter is emitted through a diagnostic macro that is invisible unless a verbosity variable is set, and that variable is in no arm’s environment. Grepping all seventeen capture logs for it returns zero hits. So “the path was never exercised” rests on reading the source, not on a measured zero. Stated as UNVERIFIED rather than asserted.

The field was git rev-parse HEAD of the worktree the tool ran from, not the commit compiled into the exe it measured. Of 404 manifests on this machine, only 31 are checkable (recorded exe still exists byte-identical) — and 28 of those 31 name a commit their binary was never built from. 23 of 31 also disagree on branch, 11 on dirty. Across two scratch trees, seven distinct commit values over 23 arms all describe one binary, built from a branch and commit that appear in no manifest at all. Worked example from the commit: a reader of 04_animstatic would conclude it exercised 3ab322a0 — that code was never in the binary. 338 manifests are permanently unverifiable (exe rebuilt or deleted), including every golden under tests/visual/baselines.

The feature registry declares it default-OFF (RendererFeatureRegistry.h:309, doc string “Opt-in MC2_SHADOW_ENABLE=1”), and docs/tier1_env_vars.md:48 repeats it.

Three readers, two behaviours, one published default.

THREE written sources said default OFF. The registry entry (defaultOn=false, “Default-off; =1 enables”), docs/tier1_env_vars.md:210, and the reader’s own comment two lines above itself (“gate, default OFF”).

deploy_payload.py:996 used shutil.copyfile, which opens the destination "wb" — it truncates and rewrites the shared inode instead of replacing the directory entry. Measured now, by inode identity: the base mc2-win64-v0.4d-rc1 holds 28,803 files and every single one has nlink>1; the union shared with the other four is 28,803 of 28,803 — 100%. The sharpest part: every lock, lease and registry check is path-keyed — DEPLOY_ALLOWLIST, .mc2_deploy_lane.json, .smoke_leases.json, deploy_status(), deploy_lane_clash — and a hardlink is precisely the case where two paths are one object. The two big surfaces push in OPPOSITE directions and partly cancel — which is the ambient floor’s stated purpose. The concrete adopt acts only on overlay fragments carrying cementWord bit 31; the ambient floor acts only where flatLitShare < 1, and that is exactly 1 on concrete because MC2_CEMENT_LIT defaults to 0.0 (read from the reader). Disjoint pixel sets — no multiplicative compounding. Direction: the adopt widens the terrain-vs-concrete contrast; the ambient floor lifts only the terrain side and narrows it. Net: a narrower pad:ground gap than either alone.

They do compound, in the same direction, at exactly one boundary: non-cement overlay art vs the terrain beside it. The chunk terrain now has an additive ambient; the overlay layer has none (its only additive is the V1 hemisphere fill, which uploads 0.0 at stock). By this project’s own measurement, unclassified paved-overlay tiles are mc2_01 29%, mc2_03 81%, mc2_05 41%, mc2_10 58%, mc2_24 34% of paved tiles. So in daylight the ground gains ~0.03–0.044 absolute luma while every non-cement overlay fragment beside it gains zero. This is a NEW two-shader disagreement of exactly the class OVERLAY-CEMENT-ADOPT-1 landed three hours earlier to close.

Whether that new seam is VISIBLE is genuinely undetermined, and here is the one measurement that settles it. terrain_overlay.frag discards alpha<0.5 and writes opaque, so where it draws it fully replaces the chunk pixel — which would make the seam real. But the project’s own registry text also says a paved-overlay tile “KEEPS its own baked colormap albedo”, which implies the chunk pass draws the road art — which would make the seam academic. Both cannot be fully true of the same pixels, and nobody resolved which pass owns them. SETTLING MEASUREMENT: one daylight mc2_03 pose, captured 2×2 over MC2_TERRAIN_AMBIENT_FLOOR={0,default} × MC2_OVERLAY_CEMENT_ADOPT={0,default}, with MC2_TERRAIN_LOD_CHUNK_DIAG=32768 to mark which pass owns which pixel. Four captures. Needs decision 11.

Also unverified and worth saying plainly: the ambient floor’s own magnitude claims (“~0.044 absolute luma”, “relief compresses only 2.3× → 2.0×”) did not survive an independent re-derivation from the shader — a reviewer’s arithmetic gives a larger relative lift on shaded ground (~+18% on fully lit flat ground, up to ~+59% at the normalLight floor of 0.367). Nobody has measured a pixel. Treat the doc’s numbers as unconfirmed.

One commit today can change whether the game STARTS or SAVES, and it is not a pixel change. gameos.cpp’s gos_GetDriveFreeSpace was rewritten: previously GetDiskFreeSpaceEx(NULL,…) with an unchecked return and an uninitialised out-param; now it queries the path, falls back to the current drive, and returns 0 if both fail, so callers take the out-of-space branch. Callers are the mechcmd2.cpp startup check and Mission::save. That is a new failure mode on a default launch and it is worth knowing before the first click-through.

THE ONE STRUCTURAL RULE THIS BATCH NEEDS, and it is worth more than any further check. (1) No contract may be a substring or regex presence test over a whole file. It must anchor to the specific construct — the AST node, or at minimum the enclosing function — or it is decoration. (2) “The thing I am looking for is ABSENT” must never route to the same bucket as “the thing I am looking for is FINE.” gate_default_agreement’s no_reader bucket, and every future skip path, must be a FAIL or a counted, surfaced debt — never silence.

A static prop recipe is a frozen snapshot that is not invalidated when a building becomes ineligible via a state-to-state gesture, flash or activity — so a live recipe holds a stale pose. Black outlines: the shadow-caster feed walks the full registry, visibility- and eligibility-independent, and is DEFAULT-ON — so an animating building casts a shadow from its mission-load pose. Sunk turrets: turrets have no ground-snap at all, and the recipe bakes the raw .ase rest pose pre-snap.

OPEN — NOT CONFIRMED. These are ranked hypotheses with default-ON reachability proven at source, not a diagnosis. Settled by decision 11: list the buildings on mc2_03, then a one-frame shadow-caster A/B.
Building LOD swaps were the leading explanation for prop pop and were reasoned from repeatedly.
IT CANNOT FIRE. Building LOD is pinned to 0. Every chain of reasoning that routed through it is void.

RETRACTED. The memory file asserting the mechanism is stale and should not be trusted until corrected. Worth noting how this survived so long: it was in a memory file, and memory files are not covered by any contract.
The one-sided-safe B-spline was the designed cure; mc2_17 and mc2_10 were the same tile-locked defect.

The B-spline was FALSIFIED OFFLINE before it was built: it moves the waterline 5.1 wu against the ~100 wu required. mc2_17 is NOT tile-locked (staircase index 0.260 vs a 0.222 floor); mc2_10 IS (0.737). Different defects. The real mc2_17 mechanism is the drape cap handing the edge to the depth test at 128 wu on 66.7% of the waterline.

RETRACTED · OPEN
A general principle now kills a whole FAMILY of cures: anything budgeted in elevation units inherits 1/|grad| and is weakest exactly where the defect is worst. Blocked on decision 1 (displacement or faceting?).
Tree silhouettes were suspected to be baked into the art.
Proven NOT baked art — 2,088 positions measured under all 8 orientations. The real finding: trees carry no directional light at all, so sunColor * ndl is identically zero.

FALSE LEAD CLOSED · OPEN
A real, specific, mechanism-level cause now exists with no cure attached. This is the same shape as the vehicle defect (numLights==0 → vec3(1,1,1)) that VEHICLE-LIGHTING-PATH-1 addressed — which makes it a strong candidate for the same treatment, and a strong candidate to have the same untested night direction.

blocks.html:
Two mechanical blocks are now live and tested, and both exist because a written rule was violated repeatedly. (1) Game launches are hard-blocked by a PreToolUse hook. You reported five separate times that agent launches steal your mouse, keyboard and focus. Every prompt-level rule was violated anyway, so the block is now mechanical. It is not being worked around — this update was written entirely from source, git, and offline file inspection, and the hook fired once during it (on a command that merely named the binary to read its timestamp) and was obeyed. (2) git add -A / git add . / git commit -a are blocked, because several lanes share worktrees and a sweep stages other lanes’ work. That happened twice.

The honest cost of block (1), stated plainly: it is now the binding constraint on the project. Every pixel-changing change on this page is UNVERIFIED because of it, and no amount of further source reading will change that — the remaining questions are questions about pixels. That is what decision 11 is asking you to unblock, once, supervised.

What this update did NOT do — stated so it is not mistaken for coverage. Nothing was built and nothing was launched. Every pixel statement in §20 is derived from shader and C++ source. No luma number on this page was measured by anyone this session. A clean build of the tip was not attempted: the merge audit deliberately did not stash, because three lanes’ uncommitted work is sitting in the canonical worktree and stashing it is the exact hazard being audited. So “no line was dropped” is proven; “the merged tree compiles” is not. The contract audit injected against 6 of 98 rows and did a structural census of the rest — the older checks are unexamined, and the identifier-in-a-comment defect appearing three times suggests a systematic comment-stripping audit of all 73 tree-inspecting checks would pay. Binary fingerprinting covered engine binaries only; editor and tool executables were not checked, and three mod installs carry no fingerprint banner at all. Finally, a build from the canonical worktree right now would be stamped BUILT-FROM-DIRTY-TREE and its manifest src_commit suffixed -dirty — though the dirty edits themselves add no default pixel change (two are comment-only; the rest are guarded by an env var that is unset).

blocks.html: 21b. Available but OFF — one of these is a real measured night-lighting defect

rows.html: SPOTLIGHT-DIRECTION-1. Two coordinate-space defects at the building / guard-tower spotlight registration site. TG_Light::direction was never set, so it kept its init() default of (0,0,0) — and for POINT/SPOT lights that field is a position, not a direction, so every CPU-baked vertex was lit as though the lamp sat at the world origin instead of on its own building. This is not latent: measured on the deployed build, mc2_10 at night consumed 4,310,486 active POINT/SPOT lights in the CPU bake over 15 s, and 3,995,686 of them — 92.7% — still had direction (0,0,0). mc2_01/03/24 measured zero because these lights are night-gated.

MC2_SPOTLIGHT_DIRECTION_FIX
OFF — deliberately, because the correction changes default night appearance on mc2_10. This one wants your eyes: it is a real defect with a written fix sitting behind a switch.

LIGHT-ROW-PURE-1. One pure producer for object light rows, replacing a mutate-the-shared-list / gather / restore dance. Byte-identity is the acceptance bar and is proven offline across every class policy and light count 0..42 — but not in-engine, because the harness links no engine and launches are blocked.

MC2_LIGHT_ROW_PURE
OFF (opt-in). Flip criterion is written down: one run with MC2_LIGHT_ROW_PURE_VERIFY=1 reporting checked>0 mismatched=0.

BACKEND-DEFAULT-PARITY-1. One gate, two readers, opposite defaults: the GL reader defaulted the sky-exclusion guard ON, the Vulkan one defaulted it OFF, so on an unset environment VK fog painted over sky pixels GL excluded. Now a single reader. Does not affect a default GL launch — it only bites with MC2_VK_POST_FOG_NATIVE=1.

MC2_SKYBOX_FOG_EXCLUDE
ON (unchanged; the VK reader was the bug)

sections.heading: Reference — lanes & efforts, the full session log (71 rows; nothing here needs a verdict)

blocks.html: Every lane run in this session, in rough chronological order: what it was sent to do, what it actually found, its commits, the gates it touched with their current default re-read from the C++ reader at the moment this page was generated, and its verdict. Lanes that shipped no code are included deliberately — several of them produced this session's most valuable findings, because refuting a premise is a result. Nothing here was pushed; all commits are local to claude/nifty-mendeleev.

Provenance limit, stated plainly. This lanes log was assembled while sibling lanes held the shared worktree dirty (a key engine source uncommitted by another lane) and while a foreign smoke lease was live on the deploy path. A build made under those conditions embeds MC2_BUILD_GIT_DIRTY=1 and its captures are unattributable, so this lane captured no new images and added none. Every image on this page remains the one attributable set REVIEW-ALLPOSES-1 captured from a clean-fingerprint exe. Re-capture is the first thing to do once the tree settles.

Read verdicts precisely. APPROVED BY USER means the user saw it and said yes — do not regress it. REJECTED BY USER means the user saw it and said no — do not revive it or present it as a candidate. DISPROVEN means the lane refuted its own premise, which is a real result and not a failure. FIXED without an approval tag means agent-verified only, user click-through still pending.

⚠ REVIEW-LANES-LOG-2 CORRECTION — three “no code exists” claims from the audit were false. Each of the following had already shipped when it was reported missing: foliage alpha-test shadows (landed in June and default-ON — the “no alpha discard” premise is true only of the depth shader, and the residual defect is a stale justification comment); the LOD flash cure; and the pool consumers. Absence of a lane's memory is not absence of code — each was confirmed present by reading source. This is the same failure shape as the status-doc staleness noted below, which is why §0 and the gate column are rebuilt from source at render time and never read from a document.

lanes.name: SHORELINE-STAIRCASE-FIX-1
lanes.sent: Fix FAIL #1: water outline snaps to the terrain tile grid (~140px steps) at mc2_10 top-down.
lanes.found: Overturned the cooked-SDF premise: a cooked EDT can never equal the rendered bilinear waterline, and mc2_10 ships no shoreline_mask sidecar, so the already-wired MC2_WATER_SHORE_MASK path was inert — which is why the prior fix measured A==B. Real cause: the shore alpha ramp is only 1-2px wide.

lanes.name: SHORELINE-GEOMETRY-1
lanes.sent: Re-open of FAIL #1 after the user rejected the feather fix ("still looks terrible... a literal stair step?").
lanes.found: Overturned its predecessor: the "too-narrow alpha ramp" diagnosis is wrong. The stock heightfield is terraced, so the thickness iso-contour degenerates onto the tile lattice — widening alpha blurs a riser but cannot bend it. Also corrected the sentinel reading: the prior lane cited a low struct_delta as success, but the golden encodes the staircase, so low meant nothing moved.

lanes.name: RUNWAY-EDGE-BLEND-1
lanes.sent: Fix FAIL #6: runway/pad cement edges render as hard full-tile stairstep cliffs.
lanes.found: Overturned its own tasking pointer — the live terrain renderer is the LOD-chunk path, not the indirect path the brief named, so an indirect-only fix produced zero change. Rev-1 then measured as an erosion that dissolved the visible apron margin (mean dLum -6.55).

lanes.name: RUNWAY-EDGE-DILATE-1
lanes.sent: Redo of #6 after the user rejected rev-1 ("gate on is worse. the answer is usually MORE concrete, not less").
lanes.found: Rev-2 dilates concrete outward instead of eroding it (+2.75 lum, 68.7% brighter edge). Honest limit recorded: solid-cement-next-to-bare tiles are rare on the available maps (mc2_01: 4, mc2_10: 0), so the effect is near-imperceptible on any bookmark we have.

lanes.name: MECH-NIGHT-SHADOW-INVERT-1
lanes.sent: Fix FAIL #7: mech night shadows render BRIGHTER than the ground under them.
lanes.found: Ruled out the legacy blob path entirely (mech3d.cpp renderShadows is skipped whenever the modern shadow path is active; MC2_GROUND_CONTACT_BLOB packs pure black and cannot brighten). Real cause: the mover-attached light pool has falloff 1.0 directly under the body, so the mech floodlights the ground beneath itself. Scope-add: palm-vs-pine is not a shader bug — the shadow depth pass has no alpha discard, so alpha-card LODs are excluded from casting.

lanes.name: CONTACT-SHADOW-ALLTYPES-1
lanes.sent: Extend the #7 contact-shadow fix to all relevant object types.
lanes.found: Ground vehicles were already covered by the original #7 commit — no change needed. Helicopters are not a separate class (isHelicopter == isAirborne) and were the one real gap: full-strength contact-AO was glued to the ground under a hovering helo, so an altitude fade was added. Buildings deliberately skipped (would regress user-approved PAD-AREA-GLOW-1).

lanes.name: WATER-GRAZING-REFLECTION-1
lanes.sent: Fix FAIL #9: grazing water reads flat dull blue instead of reflecting bright sky.
lanes.found: Two causes, not one: reflMix = fres*strength*waveLOD erased the reflection exactly where Fresnel peaks; and reflection was already maxed but sampling a dark sky (RGB ~37 vs visible ~140). Pipeline finding worth more than the fix: the water_shore_grazing region rect targeted the foreground off-map SLAB, not the lake, so it "passed" regardless of water state and never caught this FAIL. Re-aimed and re-blessed.

lanes.name: BACKDROP-BLIT-ATTRIB-1
lanes.sent: Pin the true writer of the mc2_10 night white-horizon / black-band defect.
lanes.found: Solved it, disproving both standing suspects. The HDRI sky is correctly night-dark and is not the culprit; the static-prop batcher is off-path. The real writer is the edge-fog / OOB fog cloud bank painting a compile-time-constant day-tuned u_fogColor that is never night-dimmed. Required RenderDoc pixel-history on the pre-composite HDR scene FBO, not the backbuffer.

lanes.name: FAR-BACKDROP-TEXTURED-LIGHT-1
lanes.sent: Attribute and design a fix for fullbright night tree impostors / far-ridge black band.
lanes.found: Overturned the shared-light-slot premise: the object light is fine, the stale per-vertex base_light is the fault (far LODs register through a positions-only transform, so perVertexARGB is never re-baked for night). Explains why peer commit 73755184 was a proven no-op. Deliberately shipped no code — the fix is regression-sensitive and was unverified.

lanes.name: FAR-BACKDROP-TEXTURED-LIGHT-1-IMPL-1
lanes.sent: Implement and verify option A (shader base_light night substitution) from the design above.
lanes.found: The white horizon "impostors" are not on the static-prop path at all: exaggeration turned buildings solid red while the impostors stayed pure white, and the RenderDoc event is the fullscreen tonemap composite, not impostor geometry. Code is correct and safe but cannot touch the defect; gate stays OFF. RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (FALSE-CONCLUSION-RETRACT-1): this entry also read "submit_trees=0 at this pose" as corroboration, and claimed the lane had "disproved its own design's root cause". Both are withdrawn. submit_trees is a dynamic-submit-path counter that registry-replayed props never tick, so 0 is the healthy steady state and proves nothing; the exaggeration test is what carries the impostor conclusion. The design's stale-perVertexARGB root cause was never actually tested — re-tested at mc2_03 on 2026-07-30 it is NOT the cause of anything observable there (no near-vs-far base_light asymmetry; the gate is a distance-ramped ambient doubler, and mc2_03 is a day mission so a skipped night bake cannot show). Status: untested where it could apply, not disproven.

lanes.name: DEFERRED-BATCH-7
lanes.sent: Deferred sweep: shadow seam/softness, light-cone anchor, ghost light, shoreline.
lanes.found: Overturned the ghost-light premise: it is neither the additive cone glow nor the pool light, but an opaque cream folded-plane cone mesh drawn only by the coalesce multidraw path. Item-6 black band: the albedo debug view does not repaint it, so it is not chunk terrain — it is real geometry drawn pure black, unchanged by ~10 gates.

lanes.name: DEFERRED-BATCH-8C
lanes.sent: Identify the mc2_10/212019 "cream wedge" cone leaf; verify the peer backdrop fix.
lanes.found: Overturned batch-7's cone hypothesis: the wedge is L_SpotLight, a legitimate textured 16-vert lamp head with isSpot=0 that must not be skipped; added a DO-NOT-WIDEN invariant. Also disproved peer commit 73755184 by A/B on one exe — the ridge stays pure black, and its premise ("gos_vertex tint paints the whole ridge") is contradicted because the ridge is textured.

lanes.name: GHOST-LIGHT-VISIBILITY-1
lanes.sent: Stop light cones rendering on movers the player cannot see.
lanes.found: The in-code note "visible IS the fog-of-war predicate" is wrong — setVisibility(true,true) fires on every contact branch including sensor-blip-only. Also overturns DEFERRED-BATCH-8C, which called the 212019 wedge resolved lamp-head geometry: MC2_LIGHT_CONE_GLOW=0 proves it is an additive cone glow. Wrong turn recorded: a blanket staleness guard killed all building cones.

lanes.name: GHOST-CONE-VERIFY-4
lanes.sent: Verify whether ghost cones are fixed, or whether the user's images were stale.
lanes.found: The user's images were not pre-fix — they came from dirty, unattributable builds. A clean build shows all four poses clean. Found the third, ungated emission the prior lane missed: cone GEOMETRY emitting at a hardcoded 0xffffffff regardless of fade alpha. Flipping the fix default-ON caused a regression ("one of the smokes now has no mech lights on").

lanes.name: VISIBILITY-SEMANTICS-1
lanes.sent: Separate the four different jobs the single visible flag was doing.
lanes.found: The smoke runner does env.setdefault("MC2_FORCE_ALL_VISIBLE","1"), so every default smoke and capture is structurally incapable of showing this bug class. In the measured trace, visible carries zero information (1 in every column), and sensorLevel is written only inside isOnGui while gvehicl never passes 5 — so any sensorLevel>4 predicate is dead for all vehicles. That is the "no mech lights" mechanism. 28 hidden enemies leak light.

lanes.name: VIS-SEMANTICS-FINISH-2
lanes.sent: Make MC2_VIS_SEMANTICS actually reach the binary.
lanes.found: The audit's claimed mech3d.h breakage does not exist — it compiles; nobody had rebuilt. The stale-emitter turn guard was still consulting the parked gate. Critically: tests/visual/bookmarks/mc2_10.json is unusable — three provisional poses framing bare terrain, byte-identical in both arms while 4801 stale rejects logged. This is how GHOST-CONE-VERIFY-4 "passed".

lanes.name: FORCE-ALL-VISIBLE-1
lanes.sent: Provide a gate that defeats visible/alpha-fade/sensorLevel hiding for automated runs.
lanes.found: Landed MC2_FORCE_ALL_VISIBLE as an explicit, named gate rather than an implicit runner default — the implicit setdefault was what blinded the capture harness to the whole visibility bug class.

lanes.name: EDGE-LIGHT-BILLBOARD-CULL-1
lanes.sent: Fix FAIL #8: edge lights pop out by view angle.
lanes.found: Self-falsified and superseded. Claimed the lights are flat quads being backface-culled; they are prisms and nothing is culled. The one surviving finding is a measurement one: night light pools drift ~6.8% run-to-run, so two gate-ON runs differ more than ON-vs-OFF, making naive full-frame A/B meaningless.

lanes.name: LIGHT-BILLBOARD-GPU-1
lanes.sent: Redo FAIL #8 after its predecessor was falsified.
lanes.found: Predecessor wrong on both counts: the fixtures are 6-vert/7-face triangular prisms with a horizontal emissive top cap, and nothing is backface-culled. Real mechanism is sub-pixel collapse of that horizontal cap at grazing angles. Failed first attempt recorded (per-vertex-normal rotation tears the prism apart). Shipped default-ON, then the user called the result "atrociously hideous, it needs to stop".

lanes.name: RUNWAY-MARKER-LIGHTS-1
lanes.sent: Act on the user's "whatever the hell it is doing with the runway marker lights is atrociously hideous".
lanes.found: The cause was a same-session sibling gate, not a stock bug: MC2_LIGHT_BILLBOARD_FACING's min-screen-size clamp had no upper bound, pinning hundreds of regularly-spaced fixtures to constant size at every distance — dashes. Corrected its own earlier "~100% dimming" figure as a ratio artifact. Measurement lesson: 800x600 A/B systematically under-reports this bug class; capture at the user's 3840x2160.

lanes.name: LIGHT-REALISM-1
lanes.sent: Cones too hard/opaque, light not radiating, beacons emit nothing.
lanes.found: Item 3 is a starvation bug, not a look problem: the pool cap was hardcoded 64 against measured demand 142 at mc2_10, so 78 pools (55%) were dropped and which lamp lit the ground depended on list order — this explains a sibling lane's "slot reshuffle". Three separate beacon bugs found by instrumenting. Cost is the per-fragment loop, not storage: -34% average night FPS.

lanes.name: CONE-SPILL-COUPLING-1
lanes.sent: Make cones more transparent and geometrically couple the cone to its ground pool.
lanes.found: The coupling is not unimplemented — an earlier lane already built it default-ON, and it is wrong in four ways (vertical drop instead of ray-terrain intersect, arbitrary 200-unit clamp, radius never derived from spread, no miss rejection). The authorized file is downstream of the geometry the fix needs: TG_Light carries no aim on the building path. Also corrected the brief: 0.55 is variant A; the user's baseline B is 0.40.

lanes.name: VEHICLE-NIGHT-LIT-1
lanes.sent: mc2_10 night: three trucks render near-black while everything around them is lit.
lanes.found: Lead hypothesis disproven. The frame-mismatch fix changes nothing on the trucks, and magenta exaggeration proves gos_tex_vertex_lighted "owns almost no pixels in this scene" — a different program paints them. Shipped the real latent bug it found, default-OFF.

lanes.name: VEHICLE-NIGHT-LIT-2
lanes.sent: Name the program painting the dark truck, confirm it, fix it.
lanes.found: Overturned lane 1's premise. RenderDoc pixel history names terrain as the sole writer; gos_tex_vertex, gos_tex_vertex_lighted, mech.frag and the static-prop batcher are all disproven as the painter. Fixed an unrelated SetLightsOut one-way latch found on the way.

lanes.name: VEHICLE-BAKED-TRUCK-3
lanes.sent: Test the "trucks are baked into the terrain burn-in" hypothesis.
lanes.found: Hypothesis dead: both the stock 1536² and the deployed 4x mc2_10 burn-ins contain zero man-made content of any kind. Replacement hypothesis: the dark object is runway/paved-road overlay art. Separately recorded that MC2_TERRAIN_DEBUG_MODE and MC2_TERRAIN_LOD_CHUNK_DIAG are silently inert on the v0.3 exe.

lanes.name: VEHICLE-SELFLIT-5
lanes.sent: Test whether MC2_LEGACY_LIT_MC2_FRAME fixes vehicle self-lighting.
lanes.found: The gate changes zero pixels on the truck (0 of 7000 px in the box) though it demonstrably armed elsewhere; its only real effect is brightening one ground pool, a possible regression. Decisively: a live engine debug mode shows the complained-about objects are static props, not GVAppearance vehicles — overturning the shared premise of lanes 1, 2, 4 and its own tasking.

lanes.name: PROP-SELF-SHADOW-1
lanes.sent: Building props do not self-shadow; they read flat and cardboard-like.
lanes.found: No new code was needed — props explicitly opt out of self-shadow by design, baked light is per-LEAF constant rather than per-vertex, and calc_light has no occlusion term anywhere. The remedy is composing two existing default-OFF gates. Structural proof offered: RECEIVE-only changes are 100% darker pixels and zero brighter, which only an occlusion term can do. Found the blocker to ever defaulting it ON: alpha-test fences self-shadow as solid slabs.

lanes.name: PROP-SHADOW-ENABLE-2
lanes.sent: Land the alpha-shadow class; flip MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE and MC2_SSAO ON.
lanes.found: The GBuffer encoding has spare room — no bit-packing needed, reducing the design to 3 files and ~14 lines. Then blocked twice: static_prop.frag was claimed by a sibling lane, and an uncommitted gos_terrain_indirect.cpp meant no clean fingerprint was obtainable.

lanes.name: PROP-NIGHT-LIGHT-3
lanes.sent: Land the alpha-shadow class; flip shadow/SSAO ON; props dark at night.
lanes.found: The inherited 0.375 encoding value was wrong and not a no-op — it exits the shoreline shaders' continuous water band (0.15-0.35); landed 0.1875 instead. The brief's GetARGBHighlight() mechanism is falsified (it is the selection highlight). Static props never see point or spot lights at all. Root-cause candidate: TreeAppearance::update writes terrain light into the AMBIENT slot and deactivates the sun, while BldgAppearance writes the SUN slot.

lanes.name: DROPPED-ITEMS-1
lanes.sent: Four dropped items: world-shadow asymmetry, foliage shadows, LOD impostor flash, pool consumers.
lanes.found: Three of four premises refuted from git ancestry: foliage alpha-test shadows already shipped 2026-06-16 and are default-ON; the LOD-flash mechanism exists but is default-OFF with a misaligned band; pool consumers were already closed. Item 1 root cause found and it is real: the shadow matrices use the 15°-clamped sun while the shadow_screen back-face guard dots the RAW unclamped sun — and mc2_10 alone has LightDirPitch 180 (sin=0), which predicts the map-specific asymmetry.

lanes.name: SHADOW-SUNCLAMP-1
lanes.sent: Act on DROPPED-ITEMS-1's unclamped-sun finding and fix the reported world-scale shadowed-half / unshadowed-half split on mc2_10.
lanes.found: The handed-over root cause was refuted by its own A/B. Three wide mc2_10 night poses plus a liveness arm came back byte-identical gate ON vs OFF (sunclamp_center_wide hashes ea1688351a3d60a7 both ways) — because the NdotL guard only exists in sampleDynamicShadow, on the mech path, and terrain/grass/decals early-out before ever reading lightDir. The lane then located the real mechanism on the terrain path: shadow.hglsl resets normal=(0,0,1) under MC2_SHADOW_STATIC_BANDFIX_V2 (default ON) before the guard, so on mc2_10 (LightDirPitch 180) NdotL ≈ 0 < 0.05 and terrain sun shadows are suppressed globally while props/mechs keep theirs. Handed to TERRAIN-SHADOW-GUARD-1, which confirmed it.

lanes.name: LOWS-CLUSTER-1

lanes.name: PROP-LIGHT-CLASS-4
lanes.sent: Fix the tree-vs-building prop light-class bug, and flip MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE default ON.
lanes.found: Both halves failed, and the failure is the finding. (a) MC2_LIGHTING_DEBUG_VIEW=sun shows every static prop is black at night, buildings included — the predicted tree-vs-building differential does not exist. Worse, the truck's own sun term (49.0) is higher than the building's (16.0), the opposite of the prediction. RETRACTED: this row previously concluded “the dark-truck complaint is real but it is ALBEDO: the truck texture is 3.3× darker than the building texture”. The user refuted this from the actual textures and is correct — the 3.3× figure was a region-MEAN artifact (a truck fills a fraction of its measurement rect; a building fills its own). Masked re-measurement on the source art gives trucksprop.tga = 85.9 mean luminance vs a 787-texture corpus median of 86.2 (49th percentile, dead average) and buildings at 101-121 — a ~1.2-1.4× ratio, not 3.3×. (truck.tga at 37.2 is the MOBILE VEHICLE asset, not this static prop.) The cause is the lighting path; the defect is OPEN. (b) The fence self-shadow blocker did clear, but RECEIVE ON changes only 0.003-0.10% of pixels at every pose — the promised building self-shadow benefit could not be demonstrated at all.

lanes.name: EDGE-LIGHT-EMISSION-1
lanes.sent: Make runway/taxiway edge lights and beacons actually read as lit at night.
lanes.found: Shipped fbef958e, and CONE-SPILL-GRADE-1 later graded it a correct, real fix: the GPU static-prop path was passing false, 0.0 into get_base_light(), forcing the daytime arm always (+17.1 mean luminance, 100% of pixels brighter at the one noise-clean pose). But it must not be flipped on as-is — the emission is additive against an already near-saturated night ambient (~196/255), and a 4× exaggeration produced only +17.27 vs +17.14, the signature of a term already saturating.

lanes.name: TERRAIN-SHADOW-GUARD-1
lanes.sent: Land and capture-confirm the terrain-path fix for the NdotL-guard-on-raw-sun mechanism SHADOW-SUNCLAMP-1 located but could not land.
lanes.found: Confirmed by capture, not by argument. With the gate OFF, MC2_LIGHTING_DEBUG_VIEW=shadow renders the terrain shadow-factor buffer as featureless saturated white — 70.0% of the frame above 250/255 on sunclamp_center_wide, the literal return 1.0 early-out firing for every terrain pixel. With the gate ON that falls to 2.9% and relief-following terrain shadow structure appears (69.4%→28.1% on sunclamp_relief_ne). The fix landed broader than briefed — inside calcShadow/calcDynamicShadow, so it also covers decal, grass and terrain-overlay frags. Purely subtractive: 0.00% of pixels brightened in any pose. Beauty-frame magnitude is modest at night (max channel delta 4-14/255) because night ambient dominates.

lanes.name: PERF-HARNESS-TRUTH-1
lanes.sent: Fix the performance harness so GPU/fragment-bound cost is visible, and deliver the light-grid frame-time table LIGHT-CLUSTER-PERF-1 owed.
lanes.found: The inherited diagnosis was false on both counts — no window consumer reads MC2_SMOKE_MODE, and the 10 ms throttle is OS show-state-driven, not harness-driven; with a visible window the two arms still measured within 0.2%. The real cause: the harness reported CPU-side DrawScreen zone duration, which cannot show GPU fragment cost because GL submission is async — raising the per-fragment loop 4× genuinely did not move CPU time. Separately MC2_LOG was never set, so all nine .game.log files were zero bytes: the runs were not merely wrong, they were unverifiable. Once fixed (true frame-interval timing + visible window + receipt verification), the light grid lands at or slightly below the cap=64 baseline (night_busy p50 6.679→6.481 ms, −3.0%) and MC2_LIGHT_REALISM costs nothing measurable.

lanes.name: PAVED-OVERLAY-CLASS-1
lanes.sent: Close the classification gap ROAD-OVERLAY-LIGHT-1 found — roads/runways on non-cement slots never reaching the cement classify chain.
lanes.found: Classification gap closed 100% on all 5 maps (residual 0 tiles baked). Within-pavement uniformity improved on 13/15 poses, strongest at the user's own mc2_10 pose (sd 82.50→67.83, −17.8%). But the mean tone offset did not uniformly converge: it closes 50-94% where pavement was darker than cement, and widens by up to 483% where pavement was already brighter — because once both are flat-lit the residue is pure albedo, which no lighting-side lever can reach. (This was previously cited as “the same wall PROP-LIGHT-CLASS-4 hit on trucks”; that cross-reference is RETRACTED — the truck finding was a region-mean artifact and is withdrawn. The pavement-albedo residue here is a separate, independently measured result and stands on its own.) Mode 2 (albedo swap) is deliberately not recommended: it is the same class of change the user has twice rejected.

lanes.name: CONE-SPILL-GRADE-1
lanes.sent: Adversarially grade two lanes (CONE-SPILL-COUPLING-1, EDGE-LIGHT-EMISSION-1) that shipped code and died without ever being reviewed.
lanes.found: c1f98b45 is REGRESSIVE and is now default-OFF. It deletes 7 of the 9 night ground light pools on mc2_10 (POOLS_KEPT 9/9 → 2/9) in exchange for moving the 2 survivors by 7 world units and removing a 200.0f clamp that fires 0/9 times. Cause: stock fixtures are authored near-horizontal (14.9 units of drop over a 167.8-unit beam) so the ray/terrain intersection almost never lands on ground, and the miss-rejection wrongly counts buildings (absent from the heightfield) and border terrain as misses. It was riding an unregistered, undocumented, default-ON gate (MC2_LIGHT_CONE_NODES) with no gate of its own. EDGE-LIGHT-EMISSION-1 by contrast is a real fix, but saturating — see its row.

lanes.name: NIGHT-TAGS-GREEN-1
lanes.sent: Implement a scoped Hot-Green-only mode for MC2_STATIC_PROP_NIGHT_TAGS, on the premise that Hot Green tags are exclusive to runway/beacon fixtures.
lanes.found: The premise is false, and the lane refused to build on it. Of 738 meshes carrying Hot Green (0xff00ff00) in data/tgl/*.ase, only 8 are beacon/runway fixtures — the other 730 are buildings (barracks, palaces, city blocks, HPG, turrets). The shader says so itself at lighting.hglsl:118: Hot Green — Building Base Lights. Cross-checked in data: of 274 .ini files declaring HotGreenRGB, only 4 use it as a beacon emission colour; 270 use it as a building base glow. A green-only mode would relight ~270 building types to fix ~8 fixture types — a larger blast radius than the all-branch gate it was meant to narrow, aimed straight at the user's separate over-lit-buildings complaint.

lanes.name: CAPTURE-DETERMINISM-1
lanes.sent: Characterise and where possible fix the run-to-run nondeterminism in mc2_10 captures that had been invalidating pixel-A/B evidence across many lanes.
lanes.found: Reproduced the problem worse than briefed: up to 27.3% of pixels differing across three launches with byte-identical env. Found and fixed one real cause — code/mechcmd2.cpp:2245 computed frameLength from the real measured framerate even under MC2_SMOKE_FIXED_TIMESTEP, so movers integrated a different dt each launch; pinning it dropped lance_close noise 20.4%→0.269%. Raising settle frames 30→150 cut saved_204937 23.4%→15.5% but never reaches zero. A third source remains open and unpinned (12.4-15.5%): mc2_10 captures are still not reproducible. Sim/render frame skew and streaming/LOD were explicitly refuted as causes.

lanes.name: LIGHT-REALISM-FLIP-1
lanes.sent: Decide whether MC2_LIGHT_REALISM should flip default-ON, by grading variant B against the user's four night-lighting complaints.
lanes.found: Three of the four complaints (feathered cones, spill continuity, LIGHT SOURCE-like beacons) are convincingly solved. The fourth is measurably worsened. MC2_LIGHT_REALISM_POOL_SPILL=2.2 scales farDistance for every pool light uniformly, including near-camera mover lights, and hot-pixel area explodes at lance_close from 0.360% to 8.250% — 23×; at the user's own grading poses 11× and 6.3×. The proposed cure (spare mover lights) was handed to POOL-SPILL-STATIC-1, which proved it inert. Half this lane's matrix never ran: the A: volume hit 0 bytes free and 12 of 14 PNGs in one arm were written zero-byte.

lanes.name: POOL-SPILL-STATIC-1
lanes.sent: Implement LIGHT-REALISM-FLIP-1's prescribed cure — apply pool spill to static lights only, sparing mover lights — and verify it removes the blowout.
lanes.found: Implemented, proven INERT, and reverted. MC2_LIGHT_POOL_DUMP=1 receipts at the user's exact complaint poses show the light rows by class are {other: 1684, bldg: 81} — zero mech, zero gv. lightIsMover() never returns true there, so the blowout is caused entirely by static/untagged lights and the mover carve-out cannot touch it. Uniform-2.2 and static-only-2.2 are numerically indistinguishable at lance_close (7.834% vs 8.288% hot area — the “fix” is fractionally worse). A dose-response sweep then found the actual lever: POOL_SPILL=1.3 keeps the cone and beacon wins whole while cutting blowout from 8.29% to 1.27%.

lanes.name: BEACON-FIXTURE-ID-1
lanes.sent: Implement an exact discriminator so stock night emission can be scoped to runway/beacon fixtures and not buildings.
lanes.found: The brief's proposed discriminator was refuted before it was built. “Saturated-primary Hot*RGB” matches 503 of 773 stock .ini files — useless — because mclib/bdactor.cpp:813-819 defaults undeclared HotGreenRGB to 0xff00ff00, so ~499 buildings inherit a saturated primary they never declared. The shipped discriminator adds an equality clause (all three equal AND saturated), narrowing to exactly 4 of 773 with zero building leakage. But the mechanism only delivers already-stock emission: get_base_light clamps at 1.0, so scales 1, 4 and 8 are byte-identical and the visible effect is +21/255 on an already-green beacon. The user's actual complaint is not closed by this.

lanes.name: FIXTURE-GLOW-1
lanes.sent: Build a bounded additive glow so runway/beacon fixtures read as lit light sources, verify it is safe at overview altitude, and decide its default.
lanes.found: Diagnosed why every prior emissive attempt was structurally doomed: static_prop.frag:436 multiplies lighting by albedo, so a dark lens texel dims any emissive seed. Fix is a separate additive term after the albedo multiply and fog. The first shipped design was falsified by its own measurement — a view-depth clip.w window is meaningless because MC2 changes altitude by scaling the projection, not moving the eye, so ground (~659) and overview (~800) eye-distances are nearly flat and the bound was unbounded at every altitude. Re-cut as an NDC-silhouette smoothstep: 2 px changed at 1× and at 4× strength against a 232 px noise floor. Also found stock data has no white fixture at all (runwaylight.ini is red) and that at 1:1 the glow only desaturates an already channel-max lens toward white — it cannot brighten it further.

lanes.name: NIGHT-AMBIENT-BALANCE-1
lanes.sent: Test whether inflated night ambient explains the truck-vs-building contrast complaint, and whether a default flip is warranted.
lanes.found: Night ambient is inflated — but by a different mechanism than everyone had been citing, and it does not explain the complaint. The widely-quoted “196/255 night ambient” figure is wrong: static_prop.vert:242's v_dbgAmbient is authored ambient plus two port-added fill terms, not the mission's raw ambient, which is stock-faithful at NightAmbient{Red,Green,Blue}=32. The real inflator is MC2_STATIC_PROP_IBL_SH — a day-sky HDRI probe applied at full strength at night with zero night scaling, multiplicative into albedo: bldg_left gains +54.2% luminance and white-clips on 2.76% of its pixels. Killing IBL does not fix the truck gap (truck/bldg_tower 0.590→0.609). This was previously written up as “independently confirming PROP-LIGHT-CLASS-4: it is albedo, not lighting” — that conclusion is RETRACTED. Both ratios came from the same region-MEAN rectangles, so they corroborated a shared measurement artifact, not a shared finding; masked re-measurement shows the truck texture is of median brightness (85.9 vs 86.2 corpus median). The IBL night-scaling finding above is unaffected. The truck cause remains in the lighting path and is OPEN.

lanes.name: IBL-NIGHT-SCALE-1
lanes.sent: Act on NIGHT-AMBIENT-BALANCE-1: night-scale the day-sky SH-IBL probe instead of killing it.
lanes.found: Landed the night-scaling curve strength *= mix(1.0, floor, nightFactor) with floor 0.25, chosen as the measured knee — it removes 95% of the clipping for a 13-18% brightness cost, against 29-46% for a blunt killswitch. On mc2_10 night, hard-clipped pixels on a building face fall 2.49% → 0.13% (19×). Found two linkage traps en route: u_nightFactor was silently zero unless an unrelated gate happened to be on, and the IBL strength is not the neutral 0.5 default it appears to be — data/visual_tuning.json overrides it per-mission to 0.55-0.6.

lanes.name: RUNWAY-LIGHT-MISSING-1
lanes.sent: Find out why runway-light props are missing campaign-wide, per the report that they are absent on mc2_10.
lanes.found: Nothing is missing. Nothing was ever being lost. Runtime receipts on mc2_01, mc2_10 and mc2_23 show placement-to-render agreement is exact on all three — nothing culled, nothing dropped. mc2_10 simply places zero runway lights (it has 32 red / 12 green / 16 blue beacons and no runway lights at all), while 365 runway lights exist across the campaign: mc2_23 has 112 at full night, mc2_01 has 56 in daylight. Five prior lanes verified fixture work on the one map that has none of the fixture in question. On maps that do have them the lights are drawn, but read as dull amber cones because emission is clamped at 1.0 then multiplied by a dark lens albedo — a brightness ceiling on present geometry, not absent geometry. The lane also caught its own first-pass table (which claimed mc2_10 had 32) as wrong, via an ordinal off-by-one, by cross-checking the engine's runtime receipt.

lanes.name: SHADOW-DECISIONS-1
lanes.sent: Grade three shadow/AO gates (MC2_SSAO, MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE, MC2_PROP_LOD_SHADOW_CAST) against the user's building-face complaint.
lanes.found: All three recommended to stay default-OFF, each for a different reason. MC2_SSAO measures essentially zero benefit at shipped tuning — AO buffer mean 254.99/255, byte-identical at night — traced to aoRadius_ defaulting to 3.0 world units. MC2_PROP_SHADOW_RECEIVE architecturally cannot fix the complaint: a face turned away from the sun already has ndl = 0, so a shadow term multiplying it changes nothing; it moves 0.005-0.183% of pixels and only on props like aircraft, never on building faces. MC2_PROP_LOD_SHADOW_CAST landed as code but showed no demonstrable benefit across 14 day + 3 night poses — what changed were mover sprites, not tree shadows. Its identification of base_light as the culprit was itself later falsified by PROP-BASE-LIGHT-DIR-1.

lanes.name: SSAO-RETUNE-1
lanes.sent: Establish whether MC2_SSAO's zero measured benefit is a radius-tuning problem or something deeper.
lanes.found: MC2_SSAO is latent-broken, not merely off. The radius half was confirmed: aoRadius_ defaults to 3.0 world units against a 42.67 wu map cell — a mean reach of 0.87 wu, 2% of one cell — producing literally zero occlusion (0 px below 250/255). Raising it to 40 produces real structured signal at prop bases, fence lines and gantry cranes. But grading that at 1:1 overturned the “just retune it” premise by surfacing a second, independent defect: there is no blur pass at all. runSSAO is two draws, gen and apply; the only denoise is a 4-tap box spanning ±0.5 of a half-res texel, which cannot denoise a 16-sample stochastic kernel. So any radius large enough to show occlusion also shows speckled dither on flat unoccluded faces — worse than the darkening it was meant to add. A bilateral blur must land before any default-ON proposal.

lanes.name: PROP-BASE-LIGHT-DIR-1
lanes.sent: Add a directional term to static-prop base lighting to darken building faces turned away from the sun, per SHADOW-DECISIONS-1's identified root cause.
lanes.found: The inherited root cause was falsified by measurement. Built on base_light, the gate gave byte-identical output at every strength including 1.0 — which multiplies the seed by zero, and is impossible if base_light mattered. After ruling out env-drop, harness caching, wrong-shader and props-not-in-frame, the lane proved base_light is effectively ZERO on these props, day and night. The term actually lighting them is ambientTerm, the per-actor object-light ambient — orientation-free by construction, exactly the defect shape described, in a different summand. Re-pointed there it moves 2.5-6.9% of pixels, monotonic and safe. But the user's acceptance test was never demonstrated: no bookmark pose showing an actual lit-from-behind wall was ever found, and the designed foliage alpha-test exclusion does not fire (trees darken, 33,053 px on one pose).

lanes.name: GOLDEN-REBLESS-2
lanes.sent: Re-bless the visual regression goldens honestly from a deterministic, attributable build; audit pose honesty; report on a release re-cut.
lanes.found: The prior 16-entry golden registry was already entirely dead — 16/16 pointed at a deleted worktree path, so there was nothing to re-bless. Live goldens carried blessed_commit: null and no recorded env or gate state. Under a 3-run-minimum rule, 27 of 39 regions were blessed and 12 were REFUSED with measured noise floors up to 20.04% — refused rather than silently passed. Critically, v0.5.2-baseline-PROPOSED fails 32 of 39 regions (up to 96.3% pixel change), and that is real content drift from ~70 commits of night-lighting work, not noise — the same regions measure 0.0000% run-to-run. Its defining poses exist only inside a deploy install and are not version-controlled, so it is unauditable and unrecoverable. Recommendation: do not promote it.

lanes.name: DETERMINISM-RATCHET-2
lanes.sent: Make the capture-determinism ratchet actually catch nondeterministic regions, attribute the residual mc2_10 drift, and close gate-hygiene issues voiding verifications.
lanes.found: The ratchet was blind by directory depth. It globbed r1/*.png, one flat level, while captures nest two deep as crops/<bookmark>/<region>.png — so on a real 234-PNG, 3-run noisy set it saw 0 files, printed SKIP and exited 0. Fixed with rglob, empty-set-now-fails, and all-pairs --min-runs 3; it then caught all 12 regions GOLDEN-REBLESS-2 refused plus 2 more that lane had wrongly blessed, because that lane only ever compared r1-v-r2 and r1-v-r3, never r2-v-r3. Also overturned the registry-debt numbers by an order of magnitude: ENV_DROP_RISK is 620, not the 101 previously believed (830 unregistered, 726 undocumented, 5 genuine ghosts). Attributed the residual mc2_10 drift to a single target-acquisition divergence at t=34.1 s (one Centipede, id 711); mover iteration order and ASLR were explicitly refuted.
